pdf_title: Loyalty-SMOTE: Data Synthesis Algorithm for Effective Imbalanced Data Classification
srcdet: Table 1 assigns sources per group only: group 1 (30 binary) 'UCI/KEEL' without per-dataset attribution (names such as glass5, vowel0, ecoli-0-1-3-7_vs_2-6, yeast-0-3-5-9_vs_7-8 match KEEL naming, but the paper does not say which come from which); group 2 (5), group 3 (9) and group 5 (10) from Kaggle; group 4 (5 multiclass) from UCI.
crit: Only that the paper 'uses four groups of commonly used imbalanced datasets'; group 3 described as 'large-scale datasets and 2 small-scale datasets' (for runtime), group 5 as 'high-dimensional' and 'large-scale' datasets.
split_protocol: single 7:3 train/test split (no repetitions or CV stated)
ir_definition: IR = N_majority / N_minority, where N_majority and N_minority are the sizes of the majority and minority classes (Eq. 14); for multiclass, the class with the most instances is majority and the class with the fewest is minority.

evidence.quote: Our results demonstrate that Loyalty-SMOTE achieved superior performance across multiple metrics on both binary and multiclass UCI datasets. For 30 binary datasets, it achieved the highest scores in 26 datasets (87%) for F1-score
To evaluate the performance of the Loyalty-SMOTE algorithm, this paper uses four groups of commonly used imbalanced datasets. The sources and details of these datasets are shown in Table 1.

notes: Page numbers are printed journal page numbers (pages 1-16). Text says 'four groups' but Table 1 lists five groups. Table 1 says group 3 has 9 datasets (7 large + 2 small) and Section 4.4.3 says '9 datasets in group 3', but Table 4 lists only 8 (magic04, covertype, Purchase, Satisfied, AIDS_50000, smoke, vertebal, parkinson); runtime Table 14 lists bank-full (not in Table 4) and omits parkinson. n_datasets_claimed=59 is the sum of Table 1 group counts (30+5+9+5+10); 'Bankruptcy' appears in both group 1 and group 5. Table 5 header has 'Instances' twice; the first such column appears to be number of classes (e.g., yeast 10). Typos kept as printed: 'vertebal', 'bezediris', 'imbalanced Rate'. Inconsistency: 'Fault' (Table 2) vs 'faults' (Discussion). Table 6 label conflict: text calls confusion matrix Table 6, but the group-5 description is also Table 6 and confusion matrix is Table 7. Group 1 F1 (Table 9) and Recall (Table 11) baseline columns are largely identical, and G-mean (Table 12) baseline values often equal them too. No binarisation or class-selection procedure is described for any dataset (e.g., iris, bezediris). No code or data links given. Group 2 used only for parameter sensitivity (Figs. 8-9). Eq. 14 symbols were garbled in the text layer; IR formula read as majority size over minority size from the accompanying sentence.
